purpose: Non-admission discovery of four differentiated sources for jurisdictional building-code adoption, modeled code-related annual losses avoided, global flood-defence inventory context and observed insured catastrophe event benchmarks. This registry records public source-page evidence only; it does not admit external bytes, authorize commercial use or imply model fitness.

entries.name: Preserved FEMA Building Code Adoption Tracker (BCAT) spatial extract v2
entries.provider: Public Environmental Data Partners / Environmental Data and Governance Initiative; original programme FEMA
entries.spatial_scope: United States; tracked state, local, tribal and territorial jurisdictions, subject to FEMA tracking coverage and source geometry constraints
entries.temporal_scope: Uploader says source collected 2025-12-03; archived Zenodo v2 dated 2026-06-30; adoption effective dates and current status require field-level verification
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Versioned Zenodo archive with BCAT_gepoackage.zip (1.2 GB), FEMA BCAT.gdb.zip (329.3 MB) and a metadata PDF; jurisdictional building-code adoption records, not building-by-building attributes
entries.note: Zenodo names Public Environmental Data Partners as collector, publishes CC0 1.0 metadata and lists file MD5 values; this is a third-party preserved extract of FEMA's BCAT programme, NOT proof that FEMA authored or licensed the archive under CC0. Before acquisition or reuse verify upstream FEMA terms, archive provenance, record-level vintage, jurisdiction coverage and valid date, and compute SHA-256 on exact selected file. Adoption at jurisdiction scale does not prove code compliance, year-built, retrofitting, insured replacement value or event-level vulnerability. No dataset bytes downloaded or approved for modelling.

entries.name: FEMA Building Codes Save AALs from the adoption of I-Codes (FEMA-0173)
entries.provider: U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Resilience / Risk Management Directorate
entries.spatial_scope: United States; FEMA catalogue describes local, state, regional and national aggregate outputs
entries.temporal_scope: Nationwide Building Codes Save analysis reports modeled building-code risk reduction for post-2000 construction; data.gov entry FEMA-0173 updated 2024-07, not an annual year-by-year observed claims time series
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Official FEMA XLSX `fema_building-codes-save-study-results.xlsx` linked by US catalog.data.gov record FEMA-0173; specific workbook sheets, keys, versions, currency base and hazard breakdown unverified without original file examination
entries.note: The official government catalogue identifies publication FEMA-0173, public access, FEMA publisher, links a government-works licence guidance page and supplies an XLSX resource at https://www.fema.gov/sites/default/files/documents/fema_building-codes-save-study-results.xlsx. These are MODELLED average annual losses avoided (AALA), not historical insured claims, claims frequency, independently observed loss reductions, a carrier TIV book or a vulnerability curve. They depend on Hazus and underlying modeled exposure and hazard assumptions; do not use as both training target and independent validation of a related Hazus-derived model. AALA is a scenario difference in AAL, not AAL or AEP/OEP itself. Verify source workbook table grain, dollar year, historical building stock and peril coverage, potential underlying third-party rights and selected file SHA-256 before model-use/licensing decisions. No XLSX or original source bytes acquired.

entries.name: Global Levee Database Inventory (GLDI) supporting gridded inventory
entries.provider: Global Levee Database Inventory research authors, International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction
entries.spatial_scope: Worldwide inventory of available national-scale levee records; spatial coverage and completeness vary substantially with underlying source country and inventory
entries.temporal_scope: Published November 2025; different source record dates and defence construction/upgrade vintages must remain separate
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Article advertises immediately available supplementary 0.25-degree ASCII grid and source spreadsheet; individual detailed source data available on request. Inventory aggregates 638 distinct sources in 26 languages.
entries.note: The paper's open-access article licence must not be assumed to cover each underlying national levee record. The advertised 0.25-degree grid is coarse inventory context, not bank geometry, certified flood-protection standard, crest elevation, failure probability or return-period conditional protection. Exact supplementary file/version and rights must be checked before reading or redistribution; detailed data explicitly require author contact. Do not lower location flood risk solely because the inventory indicates a nearby levee. No external data ingested.

entries.name: Insurance Council of Australia catastrophe claims data hub
entries.spatial_scope: Australia; ICA-declared catastrophes and significant events, with variable impacted regions and peril coverage
entries.temporal_scope: Historical catastrophe event register extends to 1967; live data hub updates claims figures, so pin exact as-of date and underlying release when extracting; 2025-2026 resilience report is a distinct annual product
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Event and declaration level: claim counts, incurred and outstanding insured costs, closed-rate, names/event codes and impacted regions; no policyholder records, spatial location TIV or insurer-level risk inventory
entries.note: The ICA Data Hub disclaimer explicitly prohibits commercial exploitation and reserves all copyright. Noncommercial excerpts require ICA attribution. Preserve these restrictions: publication or insurer-model calibration in commercial operations is NOT allowed by public viewing, and no source bytes/claims figures are admitted. Event losses are reported by members as claims evolve; incurred and outstanding are not ultimate gross or net loss, the declared-event selection is not complete all-peril loss experience, and figures are not independent of the underlying ICA member reporting. A separate written licence and scientific scope review would be needed for a commercial production consumer.
